name: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
description: Meta's smallest instruction-tuned Llama model. At just 1B parameters it runs on virtually any hardware — even CPUs — while still following instructions well. Ideal for edge devices, mobile, and latency-critical applications.

name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
description: Meta's 3B Llama model offers a strong quality-to-size trade-off for constrained hardware. Fits in 4 GB VRAM at 4-bit quantization, making it perfect for laptops and budget GPUs while delivering solid instruction-following quality.

name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
description: Meta's 8B parameter workhorse — widely deployed for local inference. Achieves 68.4% MMLU and 72.6% HumanEval, fitting comfortably on a single RTX 3090 or 4090 at FP16. The go-to choice for most single-GPU setups.

name: Llama 3.1 70B Instruct
description: Meta's flagship 70B model: 83.6% MMLU and 80.5% HumanEval. Requires 141 GB VRAM at FP16 but only ~35 GB at 4-bit, making it runnable on a single A100 80G or two RTX 3090s. The standard benchmark for large open-source models.

name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
description: Meta's latest 70B upgrade over Llama 3.1, with 86% MMLU, 88.4% HumanEval and 11% SWE-bench. Same VRAM footprint as Llama 3.1 70B but noticeably better at coding and agentic tasks. The best 70B class open model.

name: Llama 3.1 405B Instruct
description: Meta's largest open-source model at 405B parameters, achieving 87.3% MMLU. Requires 810 GB VRAM at FP16 — needs at least 5× H100 SXM — but ~200 GB at 4-bit. The strongest fully open LLM available.

name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3
description: Mistral AI's foundational 7B instruction model, renowned for punching above its weight. Fits in 8 GB VRAM at 4-bit, runs on virtually any consumer GPU. A great starting point for local LLM experiments.

name: Mixtral 8x7B Instruct
description: Mistral's mixture-of-experts model with 47B total parameters but only 13B active per token — delivering high quality at efficient inference cost. Achieves 71.2% MMLU. Requires ~93 GB FP16 or ~24 GB at 4-bit.

name: Mixtral 8x22B Instruct
description: Mistral's flagship MoE model with 141B total parameters and 39B active per forward pass. Scores 77.7% MMLU and 51.3% HumanEval. At 4-bit it fits in ~70 GB, making it deployable on a single A100 80G or M3 Ultra.

name: Mistral Nemo Instruct
description: Mistral's 12B model trained jointly with NVIDIA. Fits in a single RTX 4090 at FP16 and under 8 GB at 4-bit. Achieves 68% MMLU with a 128K context window — an excellent balance for single-GPU setups.

name: Mistral Large Instruct
description: Mistral's 123B flagship dense model, scoring 84% MMLU and 83% HumanEval. Comparable in quality to GPT-4 class models. Requires 250 GB FP16 but fits in ~62 GB at 4-bit — deployable on a single H100 80G.

name: Mistral Small 3.1 24B Instruct
description: Mistral's efficient 24B model from March 2025, achieving 81.5% MMLU with a vision capability. At 49 GB FP16 it fits a pair of 24 GB GPUs; at 4-bit it fits in just 12 GB. A strong all-rounder for hobbyist setups.

name: Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct
description: Qwen's 7B model that outperforms much larger models on math and coding: 84.1% HumanEval and 75.5% MATH. Fits in 8 GB VRAM at 4-bit. One of the best sub-10B open models available for coding tasks.

name: Qwen 2.5 14B Instruct
description: Qwen's 14B model offering 79.7% MMLU and 79.9% MATH — competitive with much larger models. At 28 GB FP16 it needs two 16 GB GPUs; at 4-bit it fits in a single RTX 3090 or 4090.

name: Qwen 2.5 32B Instruct
description: Qwen's powerful 32B model scoring 83% MMLU, 85.4% HumanEval, and 17.2% SWE-bench. At 65 GB FP16 it fits in a pair of A40s or H100 PCIe; at 4-bit it squeezes into a single RTX 4090 or M3 Max.

name: Qwen 2.5 72B Instruct
description: Qwen's 72B flagship: 85.3% MMLU, 86% HumanEval, 83.1% MATH, and 23.3% SWE-bench. One of the best open-source models of its size. At 4-bit it fits in ~36 GB — two RTX 4090s or a single A100 80G.

name: Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B Instruct
description: Qwen's specialized 7B coding model with 88.4% HumanEval and 83.9% MATH. Outperforms many 70B general models on code tasks. Fits in 4 GB at 4-bit — the best coding model for budget GPUs.

name: Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B Instruct
description: Qwen's top coding model: 92.7% HumanEval, 88.2% MATH, and 30% SWE-bench — matching GPT-4 class models on code. Requires 65 GB FP16; at 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090 or 24 GB GPU.

name: QwQ 32B
description: Qwen's reasoning-focused 32B model with chain-of-thought training: 91.5% HumanEval, 95.8% MATH, and 42% GAIA — competitive with much larger models. At 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090.

name: Qwen3 4B
description: Qwen's latest 4B model with hybrid thinking mode: 78.6% HumanEval and 84.9% MATH — matching Llama 3.1 8B at half the size. Fits in just 2.5 GB at 4-bit, ideal for edge deployment.

name: Qwen3 8B
description: Qwen3's 8B model with optional thinking mode: 79.4% MMLU and 88.8% MATH. Outperforms many 70B models when thinking mode is enabled. Fits in 4.5 GB at 4-bit — an excellent all-rounder for single-GPU setups.

name: Qwen3 14B
description: Qwen3's 14B model achieving 83.2% MMLU, 86.5% HumanEval, and 92% MATH — outperforming Llama 3.1 70B on math benchmarks. At 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090 or 3090.

name: Qwen3 32B
description: Qwen3's top dense model: 85.4% MMLU, 90.1% HumanEval, 94.1% MATH, 28% SWE-bench. A frontier reasoning model that fits on consumer hardware at 4-bit. Best-in-class at the 32B scale.

name: Qwen3 30B-A3B
description: Qwen3's 30B sparse MoE model with only 3B active parameters per token — delivering near-32B quality at 7B inference cost. Fits in 32 GB FP16 or 8 GB at 4-bit. Outstanding efficiency for its capability class.

name: DeepSeek R1
description: DeepSeek's flagship reasoning model: 90.8% MMLU, 96.3% HumanEval, 97.3% MATH, and 49.2% SWE-bench — matching GPT-o1. Requires 8× H100 SXM at FP16; at 4-bit fits in ~336 GB. The most capable open-source model.

name: DeepSeek V3
description: DeepSeek's 671B MoE general-purpose model: 88.5% MMLU, 91.6% HumanEval, 42% SWE-bench. Trained for a fraction of GPT-4's cost. At 4-bit fits in ~336 GB. One of the most efficient frontier-class open models.

name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 7B
description: DeepSeek R1's reasoning capabilities distilled into a 7B model: 86% HumanEval and 92.8% MATH. Punches far above its weight on math and code. Fits in 4 GB at 4-bit — the best budget reasoning model.

name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 14B
description: R1's reasoning distilled into 14B parameters: 91.5% HumanEval and 93.9% MATH. Outperforms GPT-4o on math benchmarks at a fraction of the size. At 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090 or M3 Max 24G.

name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 32B
description: DeepSeek R1 distilled to 32B: 92.7% HumanEval, 94.3% MATH, 32% SWE-bench. Near-frontier reasoning at a deployable scale. At 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090 24 GB.

name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 8B
description: DeepSeek R1's reasoning distilled into Llama 3.1 8B: 73.8% HumanEval and 89.1% MATH. Exceptional math and coding for an 8B model. Fits in 4 GB at 4-bit — best-in-class reasoning for budget hardware.

name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 70B
description: R1 reasoning distilled into Llama 3.1 70B: 95.1% HumanEval, 94.5% MATH, 77.6% MMLU. Near-R1 quality at 70B scale. Requires 141 GB FP16 or ~35 GB at 4-bit — runnable on two RTX 4090s.

name: DeepSeek Coder V2 Instruct
description: DeepSeek's 236B MoE coding specialist: 90.2% HumanEval and 29% SWE-bench. Active inference uses only ~21B parameters. Fits in 140 GB FP16 or ~35 GB at 4-bit — one of the strongest open coding models.

name: Gemma 2 2B IT
description: Google's compact 2B model punching above its weight: 55.7% MMLU. Fits in just 1.5 GB at 4-bit — the most capable sub-3B model for edge deployment and on-device inference.

name: Gemma 2 9B IT
description: Google's 9B model with exceptional quality for its size: 72.3% MMLU and 68.3% HumanEval — competitive with 70B models on many tasks. At 4-bit fits in 5 GB. One of the best sub-10B models.

name: Gemma 2 27B IT
description: Google's 27B Gemma model: 78.7% MMLU and 74.4% HumanEval. Fits in 55 GB FP16 — a single L40S or two A40s — or ~14 GB at 4-bit on a single RTX 4090.

name: Gemma 3 4B IT
description: Google's multimodal 4B model from the Gemma 3 series: 59.6% MMLU and 62.1% MATH. Supports vision inputs. Fits in 2 GB at 4-bit, making it ideal for on-device or edge AI applications.

name: Gemma 3 12B IT
description: Google's vision-capable 12B model: 74.5% MMLU, 79.2% HumanEval, and 79.5% MATH. Fits in 24 GB FP16 on a single RTX 4090 or ~6 GB at 4-bit. Strong all-rounder with native multimodal support.

name: Gemma 3 27B IT
description: Google's most capable open multimodal model: 83.2% MMLU, 82% HumanEval, and 89.2% MATH. At 4-bit fits in ~14 GB — a single RTX 4090 — with vision capability included. A remarkable value at this size.

name: Phi-3.5 Mini Instruct
description: Microsoft's 3.8B model that rivals 7B competitors: 69% MMLU and 62.8% HumanEval. Features a 128K context window. Fits in just 2 GB at 4-bit — Microsoft's most efficient small language model.

name: Phi-4
description: Microsoft's 14B model that outperforms many 70B models: 84.8% MMLU, 82.6% HumanEval, and 80.4% MATH. Trained with high-quality synthetic data. At 4-bit fits in 7 GB — exceptional performance per GB of VRAM.

name: Phi-4 Mini Instruct
description: Microsoft's compact 3.8B Phi-4 model: 67.1% MMLU and 75.4% HumanEval with strong coding ability. Fits in 2 GB at 4-bit. An ideal model for function calling and structured output on minimal hardware.

name: Llama 3.1 Nemotron 70B Instruct
description: NVIDIA's fine-tuned 70B model built on Llama 3.1 with RLHF: 85.1% MMLU and 84.1% HumanEval. Optimized for instruction-following and alignment. Requires 141 GB FP16 or ~35 GB at 4-bit.

name: Hermes 3 Llama 3.1 8B
description: NousResearch's Hermes 3 fine-tune of Llama 3.1 8B, optimized for function calling, JSON output, and agentic tasks: 67.8% MMLU. Fits in 4 GB at 4-bit. Popular choice for tool-calling applications.

name: Hermes 3 Llama 3.1 70B
description: NousResearch's 70B Hermes 3, fine-tuned for advanced function calling and agentic use: 82% MMLU. At 4-bit fits in ~35 GB. A top choice for building AI agents and tool-use pipelines.

name: GLM-4 32B
description: Zhipu AI's 32B general model: 83% MMLU, 85% HumanEval, and 20% SWE-bench. Strong multilingual capabilities particularly in Chinese and English. At 4-bit fits in a single RTX 4090.

name: GLM-Z1 32B
description: Zhipu AI's 32B reasoning model with chain-of-thought capabilities: 90% HumanEval, 92% MATH, and 30% SWE-bench. One of the strongest 32B open reasoning models. At 4-bit fits in a single 24 GB GPU.

name: Yi 1.5 34B Chat
description: 01.AI's 34B chat model with strong multilingual support: 76.8% MMLU and 65.4% HumanEval. Good at long-context understanding with 200K context window. Requires 68 GB FP16 or ~17 GB at 4-bit.

name: InternLM3 8B Instruct
description: Shanghai AI Lab's 8B model with deep reasoning: 76% MMLU and 73% HumanEval — outperforming Llama 3.1 8B on most benchmarks. Fits in 4 GB at 4-bit. Strong at Chinese and English tasks.

name: Command R+ (Aug 2024)
description: Cohere's 104B enterprise model with RAG optimization: 75.7% MMLU and 90.5% GSM8K. Supports grounded generation with citations. Requires 210 GB FP16 or ~52 GB at 4-bit for enterprise RAG pipelines.

name: Falcon3 10B Instruct
description: TII's Falcon 3 at 10B parameters: 72% MMLU and 64% HumanEval. Strong multilingual performance across Arabic, English, French and more. Fits in 5 GB at 4-bit — ideal for multilingual applications.
